sections.title: A widespread genus
sections.text: Viola includes hundreds of annual and perennial herbs, from temperate lowlands to tropical mountains. Many have simple, toothed leaves and five-petalled flowers with a distinctive lower petal; growth form and flower colour vary widely. This plate shows a low, rhizomatous violet with heart-shaped leaves and purple flowers, but it cannot be identified to species from the genus label alone.

sections.title: Edibility depends on the species
sections.text: Leaves and flowers of certain violets, including some wild species, are eaten, but that use cannot safely be generalized to every Viola or cultivar. Roots are not interchangeable with edible leaves and flowers; verify the species and part before use. The illustration depicts no food preparation or toxic feature.
